messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER: p99 latency breach detected for dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-pool-42'. p99 > 2.5s over last 5m. Paging @Olivia Chen (primary oncall). Incident INC-2026-428.

Olivia Chen: ack, looking. pulling metrics and request traces now.

Olivia Chen: quick numbers from dashboard: p95 ~ 310ms, p99 spiking to 4.1s, streaming stalls observed (chunk gaps ~ 700ms). Request queue depth for pool-42 is 178 (typical 12).

Sam Patel: assigning to runtime triage. any recent deploys to that pool?

Devon Li: noticed autoscaler has queued scale-up but warmup backlog is large. autoscaler event shows `pending_instances=3`, `warmup_inflight=3`, `expected_ready=0` per cloud metrics.

Olivia Chen: logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-14T02:03:11Z] pool=eu-west-1-pool-42 queue_depth=178 inflight=512 p99=4.12s
[2026-03-14T02:03:23Z] warmup: provisioning ok, but init_kv_cache_latency=1.8s per worker
```

Sam Patel: that init_kv cache warmup is killing first-token latencies. looks like new workers need to populate KV cache for many large-context models -> tail.

Maria Gonzales: support notes — three paying customers seeing degraded responses: AcmeInc (webhooks delayed), PayFast (payment validation streaming stalls), Tutorly (interactive chat slow). All flagged high-severity.

Kevin Turner: customer impact estimate? percent of requests failing or >2s?

Olivia Chen: rough: about 6% of requests in that pool >2s, 1.1% >5s. Request routing: heavy traffic from eu-west region tie to dedicated tenants.

Devon Li: immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce routing to this pool for tiered customers (shift non-committed traffic to fallback pool) 2) trigger emergency manual scale-up (bypass warmup if possible) 3) enable short-term prefix cache seeding for new workers 4) notify customers.

Sam Patel: executing step 1 now. routing change:
```bash
redwoodctl route update --pool eu-west-1-pool-42 --shift 30% --to-pool eu-west-1-fallback-7 --dry-run=false
```

infra-bot: route update accepted. traffic shift started — expected convergence 45s.

Olivia Chen: executing manual scale (step 2):
```bash
redwoodctl capacity scale --pool eu-west-1-pool-42 --add 6 --force-warmup=false
```

infra-bot: scale request queued. cloud provider provisioning estimate ~ 2m 30s. autoscaler note: min_cooldown enforced, manual scale allowed.

Devon Li: workaround: enable warmup seeding for the model to prepopulate KV caches from a snapshot. This will reduce per-worker init latency. Can we apply snapshot for model `rw/text-encoder-v2`?

Sam Patel: creating snapshot and pushing to pool-42 warmup hook now.

Sam Patel: warmup hook command:
```bash
redwoodctl warmup trigger --pool eu-west-1-pool-42 --model rw/text-encoder-v2 --snapshot latest
```

infra-bot: warmup trigger accepted. snapshot push in progress (estimated 45s).

Olivia Chen: good. monitoring will show queue depth drop if warmup successful. also enabling short-lived fallback model route to reduce KV size: `model-redwood-v1-quantized` for best-effort.

Maria Gonzales: sending initial customer update: "We're investigating increased latency for dedicated EU pool. We've shifted some traffic and expect improvements within 5–10 minutes. Will follow up with root cause and ETA." sending now.

Kevin Turner: good. please collect customer-specific traces to include in postmortem. we should flag any SLA credits.

Devon Li: note from autoscaler: there was a burst window at 02:01 UTC where an internal batch job triggered ~2k parallel requests for 90s. That burst saturated pool and triggered warmup churn.

Olivia Chen: can we throttle that batch back from the producer? who owns it?

Sam Patel: looks like internal-reporting job from `analytics-batch-eu`. I'll reach out to that team to throttle/replay.

Sam Patel: messaging analytics team now: "Your job caused burst to dedicated pool-42 at 02:01UTC. Can you pause/reduce concurrency for 10m?"

Devon Li: also adding a short-term autoscaler tweak: lower warmup concurrency to avoid thrash, and increase reserved burst capacity for dedicated pools. I'll apply policy change for pool-42.

Devon Li: applying policy: `autoscaler.policy.set --pool eu-west-1-pool-42 --reserved-burst=4 --warmup-concurrency=1`

infra-bot: policy change accepted. new reserved_burst=4.

Olivia Chen: visible improvement: p99 down from 4.1s -> 2.0s after traffic shift and warmup seed. queue depth trending down: 178 -> 46 in 90s. streaming stalls reduced.

Maria Gonzales: customers reporting partial restoration: AcmeInc says responses are faster, PayFast still seeing occasional stalls but improved.

Sam Patel: next steps: 1) keep traffic-shift in place until autoscaler finishes adding capacity + warmup completes 2) run retrospective to change batch job scheduling 3) add a circuit-breaker that reroutes heavy tail to quantized fallback earlier.

Olivia Chen: I'm going to stabilize and then handoff to Sam for the next 30m for remediation and postmortem prep. leaving notes: manual scale requested, warmup snapshot pushed, routing 30% shifted, autoscaler policy changed, customers notified.

Olivia Chen: handing to @Sam Patel. I will be available if needed. :white_check_mark:

Sam Patel: taking over. I'll stay on for handoff and coordinate with analytics and product for customer comms.

Sam Patel: timeline note: manual instances expected ready by 02:06 UTC (≈3m). autoscaler add will finish and then we'll revert routing shift gradually.

infra-bot: new instances reported ready at 02:06:28 UTC. warmup completed at 02:07:15 UTC.

Olivia Chen: p99 now 420ms, p95 280ms. closing incident alert window but keeping thread open for postmortem.

Maria Gonzales: I'll prepare a customer follow-up with timestamps and impact summary.

Kevin Turner: file a postmortem ticket and include remediation for warmup caching, autoscaler tuning, and batch-job rate limits. assign to eng-runtime + eng-sre.

Devon Li: noted. I'll draft immediate action items and a follow-up changelist.

Sam Patel: thanks everyone. closing active mitigation; will update postmortem draft in #incidents-tasks.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT: INC-2026-428 status=mitigated, severity=high -> monitoring.
